highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has announced Claude Opus 5, the latest and most capable model in the Claude family. Developers using Claude Code should check this announcement to understand new capabilities that may be available in their coding workflows.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.232 Released
highlights.summary: Subagent forking is now enabled by default, meaning a fork-type subagent inherits the full conversation and prompt cache for faster, context-aware task delegation. You can also now type @ in the prompt to mention and reference another Claude session by name, making multi-agent workflows much easier to manage.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.233 Released
highlights.summary: This release adds GitLab merge request URL support to the --worktree flag and the claude agents view, so teams using GitLab can now see MRs displayed as !N alongside GitHub PRs. An opt-in forward_user_identity gateway setting is also available, letting a proxy receive the signed-in user's identity as headers for better access control.

highlights.title: Maximizing the Value of Your Claude Code Sessions
highlights.summary: Anthropic's official blog post covers strategies for getting the most out of Claude Code sessions, making it a great reference for developers looking to improve their day-to-day productivity. It surfaced on Hacker News, indicating strong community interest in practical workflow advice.

highlights.title: Show HN: Graft – Claude Code Hooks That Cut Grep Tokens by 42%
highlights.summary: Graft is an open-source tool that adds smart Claude Code hooks to reduce the number of tokens consumed during file searches, reporting a 42% reduction in grep-related token usage. This is a practical community solution for developers worried about API costs or hitting context limits on large codebases.

highlights.title: Claude Code is Leaking Real Email Address as a User-Agent String in curl Commands
highlights.summary: A reported GitHub issue reveals that Claude Code was embedding the signed-in user's real email address in the User-Agent header of curl commands it generates, which is a potential privacy concern. Developers should be aware of this when using Claude Code in scripts that make HTTP requests to external services.

highlights.title: Claude Code: Zero to One – MCP, SubAgent, Hook, Images, Context & Background Tasks (Chinese)
highlights.summary: This comprehensive Bilibili tutorial walks through Claude Code from initial setup all the way to advanced features including MCP, sub-agents, hooks, image handling, and background task management with clear timestamps. It's an excellent structured reference for developers who want a full-coverage walkthrough in Chinese.

highlights.title: Learn 80% of Claude Code in 10 Minutes (2026 Tutorial)
highlights.summary: This YouTube video promises to cover the most important 80% of Claude Code features in just 10 minutes, making it ideal for developers who want a fast, high-value introduction without sitting through a long course. It's a great starting point before diving into more advanced documentation.

tips_of_the_day: Use the @ mention feature (new in v2.1.232) to reference another Claude session by name when orchestrating multi-step tasks — it keeps context flowing between agents without manual copy-pasting.
If you're working on a large codebase and burning through tokens on file searches, explore Claude Code hooks to intercept and optimize grep-style operations before they consume your context window.

Before running Claude Code scripts that make external HTTP requests, double-check the generated curl commands for unexpected headers — temporarily set a custom User-Agent in your shell config if you want to avoid exposing account details to third-party servers.
